text:
alex_support: FYI customer 842 reporting embeddings suddenly 1536-dim after we switched their pinned variant during onboarding. They expect 1024, index ingestion failing. Request ID: r-0a1b2c3d. Attached minimal repro payload.

jae_oncall: Can you paste the exact request + model name? Is this after a canary or an automated variant fallback? :eyes:

alex_support: Curl we sent: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \\
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk_cust842\" \\
  -d '{"model":"embed-lite-v2-pinned","input":"hello world"}'
```
Response snippet shows: 
```
{"embedding":[...1536 values...], "model":"embed-lite-v2a"}
```
So response is 1536. Customer expects 1024.

maria_eng: Noted. embed-lite-v2 should be 1024 historically. Did we swap variant alias? I see a deployment today.

deploy-bot: deploy: canary embed-lite-v2 -> embed-lite-v2a started by release/candidate-2026-03-15 at 3168031500. Canary 10% traffic.

alex_support: Canary was started ~5m before customer hit it. Their org is pinned to \"embed-lite-v2\" but routing may have fallen back to v2a. I reproduced locally with customer key: same result (1536). Quick repro (python SDK):
```python
resp = client.embeddings.create(model=\"embed-lite-v2-pinned\", input=\"test\")
len(resp.data[0].embedding) # => 1536
```

jae_oncall: Could be automatic compatibility fallback when reserved capacity not available or quantization profile mismatch. Can you check routing logs for that request id?

alex_support: Pulled router logs for r-0a1b2c3d: 
```
[3168032102] route-decision: org=842 model_req=embed-lite-v2-pinned pinned=true preferred=embed-lite-v2 unavailable=true fallback=embed-large-1536 reason=variant-availability
[3168032102] routed-to: embed-large-1536 host=gpu-45 zone=us-west-2
```

maria_eng: Ok that confirms fallback to a 1536-dim variant. Two likely causes: 1) our aliasing caused embed-lite-v2 to point to a larger base model variant during canary, or 2) routing policy allowed fallback to a compatible but different-dimension variant when capacity low. Both are bad for pinned customers.

ingest-bot: Indexing pipeline: index-cust842 failed: shape-mismatch error on vector batch. drop_count=3, expected=1024, got=1536.

jae_oncall: Short-term mitigation: pin the org to the explicit model variant id that has 1024 dims, or force routing policy to respect dimension compatibility. Long-term: ensure fallback candidates are dimension-compatible for embeddings.

alex_support: I applied temp pin rollback for org 842 to variant id embed-lite-v2-1024 (internal command):
```
curl -X POST https://console.redwood.ai/internal/pins \\
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer admin-svc\" \\
  -d '{"org_id":842,"model_variant":"embed-lite-v2-1024","reason":"rollback - embed dim mismatch"}'
```
Customer verified ingestion succeeded after rollback. :lock:

maria_eng: Thanks. Follow-ups: 1) Add a validation check in the routing layer to avoid cross-dimension fallbacks for embeddings. 2) Update model-catalog metadata so alias->variant mapping is explicit about embedding dimension. 3) Postmortem note and customer comms.

jae_oncall: I'll open an ops ticket to change fallback policy and add an alert for \"embedding-dim-mismatch\" errors spiking in ingestion. Also will check autoscaler decisioning that flagged original variant unavailable.

alex_support: Customer 842 accepted the rollback and asked for a timeline. I'll keep them posted. Thanks for the quick fix. :thumbsup:

maria_eng: Assigning to eng-ml for small API-level guard. I'll add a unit test to ensure model alias swaps preserve embedding schema or block aliasing if incompatible.

jae_oncall: Added ticket INC-5882 for routing guard + alerting.

alex_support: filing customer-facing summary and linking this thread. Closing once we have a timeline.

ingest-bot: svc-monitor: ingestion error rate for cust842 back to 0 after rollback.

maria_eng: Great. We'll follow up with a changelog entry about being careful with aliasing for embedding models.
